# Chart values

For: admins. You install the server with the Helm chart.

<!-- Generated by `make generate-docs` (helm-docs) from deploy/charts/vault-sync/values.yaml and chart-values.md.gotmpl. Do not edit this file. Change the `# --` comments in values.yaml or the template instead. -->

This page lists every value of the Helm chart in `deploy/charts/vault-sync`. [Install](install.md) walks through a full deployment, and the [configuration reference](configuration-reference.md) describes every `VAULT_SYNC_*` variable that the values set.

The chart has two top-level keys:

- `config` is the chart's own interface. Every `null` value (the default for optional settings) leaves its variable unset, so the server's default applies. `values.schema.json` checks `config` strictly: an unknown key (a typo such as `config.s3.forcepathstyle`), a value of the wrong type or a malformed duration fails the install. Byte sizes, counts and limits are integers, switches are booleans, and durations are Go duration strings such as `30s` or `1h30m`.
- `resources` is passed to the [bjw-s common library chart](https://github.com/bjw-s-labs/helm-charts/tree/main/charts/library/common) (5.3.0) and deep-merged over what the chart computes, so you can override or add anything that the library supports (see [Overriding the computed resources](#overriding-the-computed-resources)).

The chart creates no Secrets. Every credential is a reference to a Secret that you create, for example with cert-manager, CloudNativePG or external-secrets. The chart projects only the named keys of each Secret into the pods, as a directory (never with `subPath`), so a rotated Secret reaches the running pods without a restart.

## Shared settings

| Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `config.logLevel` | null (`info`) | `VAULT_SYNC_LOG_LEVEL` for the server and the export job: `debug`, `info`, `warn` or `error`. |

## PostgreSQL

| Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `config.database.url.value` | empty | `VAULT_SYNC_DATABASE_URL` as a plain value: a `postgres://` URL or libpq keyword/value string, without `sslcert`/`sslkey`. Use it only if it holds no password. Required, unless `config.database.url.secretKeyRef` is set; setting both fails the render. |
| `config.database.url.secretKeyRef.name` | empty | Secret holding `VAULT_SYNC_DATABASE_URL`. Set together with `config.database.url.secretKeyRef.key`. |
| `config.database.url.secretKeyRef.key` | empty | Key of that Secret. |
| `config.database.tls.clientCertificate.secretName` | empty | Secret with the PostgreSQL client certificate and key, for example a `kubernetes.io/tls` Secret from cert-manager or the one CloudNativePG creates for a user. Mounted at `/etc/vault-sync/database-client-cert`. It sets `VAULT_SYNC_DATABASE_TLS_CERT_FILE` and `VAULT_SYNC_DATABASE_TLS_KEY_FILE`. |
| `config.database.tls.clientCertificate.certKey` | `"tls.crt"` | Key of the certificate in that Secret. |
| `config.database.tls.clientCertificate.keyKey` | `"tls.key"` | Key of the private key in that Secret. |
| `config.database.tls.caCert.secretKeyRef.name` | empty | Secret with the CA bundle that signs the PostgreSQL server certificate (for CloudNativePG, the `<cluster>-ca` Secret, key `ca.crt`). Mounted at `/etc/vault-sync/database-ca` (server and export). It sets `VAULT_SYNC_DATABASE_TLS_CA_FILE`, which turns on full verification ([PostgreSQL TLS](postgresql-and-s3.md#postgresql-tls)). |
| `config.database.tls.caCert.secretKeyRef.key` | `"ca.crt"` | Key of the CA bundle in that Secret. |

## Server

The chart fixes the listen addresses: `VAULT_SYNC_LISTEN_ADDRESS` is `:8080` (port `http`), `VAULT_SYNC_METRICS_LISTEN_ADDRESS` is `:9090` (port `metrics`, which the probes and the ServiceMonitor use), and `VAULT_SYNC_SERVICE_METRICS_LISTEN_ADDRESS` is `:9091` (port `service-metrics`). Each value below sets the variable named; the [configuration reference](configuration-reference.md) describes it and its default.

| Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `config.server.maxRequestBytes` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES`. Keep it at or below the WAF's inspected body limit (1 MiB by default). |
| `config.server.writeTimeout` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_WRITE_TIMEOUT`. |
| `config.server.maxConcurrentRpcsPerUser` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_MAX_CONCURRENT_RPCS_PER_USER`. |
| `config.server.shutdownDelay` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_SHUTDOWN_DELAY`. |
| `config.server.shutdownTimeout` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT`. The chart sets the pod's `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` to the delay plus the timeout (5s + 30s when unset) plus 10 seconds, and at least 45. It refuses to render if an explicit `resources.controllers.main.pod.terminationGracePeriodSeconds` is not larger than their sum. |
| `config.server.blob.maxChunkBytes` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_BLOB_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES`. |
| `config.server.blob.maxSizeBytes` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_BLOB_MAX_SIZE_BYTES`. |
| `config.server.blob.maxUploadsPerVault` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_BLOB_MAX_UPLOADS_PER_VAULT`. |
| `config.server.blob.uploadTtl` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_BLOB_UPLOAD_TTL`. |
| `config.server.blob.uploadReclaimIdle` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_BLOB_UPLOAD_RECLAIM_IDLE`. |
| `config.server.blob.gcGrace` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_BLOB_GC_GRACE`. |
| `config.server.retention.keepAll` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_RETENTION_KEEP_ALL`. |
| `config.server.retention.keepDaily` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_RETENTION_KEEP_DAILY`. |
| `config.server.retention.purgeMarkerHorizon` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_RETENTION_PURGE_MARKER_HORIZON`. |
| `config.server.retention.overrideMinKeepAll` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_RETENTION_OVERRIDE_MIN_KEEP_ALL`. Only the `retention set` subcommand, run in a server pod, reads it ([Per-vault overrides](history-and-retention.md#per-vault-overrides)). |
| `config.server.retention.overrideMinKeepDaily` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_RETENTION_OVERRIDE_MIN_KEEP_DAILY`. Likewise read only by `retention set`. |
| `config.server.realtime.maxConnections` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_REALTIME_MAX_CONNECTIONS`. |
| `config.server.realtime.maxConnectionsPerUser` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_REALTIME_MAX_CONNECTIONS_PER_USER`. |
| `config.server.realtime.maxSubscriptions` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_REALTIME_MAX_SUBSCRIPTIONS`. |
| `config.server.escrow.recipient` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_ESCROW_RECIPIENT`: the escrow public key, an age hybrid recipient (`age1pq1…`), a string. It is public. the escrow private key goes into the export job only (`config.export.escrow`). |
| `config.server.escrow.signingKey` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_ESCROW_SIGNING_KEY`: the escrow signing public key (base64 Ed25519), a string, set together with `recipient`. It is public. its private key stays with the escrow identity. |
| `config.server.escrow.default` | null (`true`) | `VAULT_SYNC_ESCROW_DEFAULT`, a boolean: whether new encrypted vaults have escrow unless their owner turns it off. |
| `config.server.escrow.retiringKeyIds` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_ESCROW_RETIRING_KEY_IDS`: comma-separated ids of escrow keys being rotated away from, which escrow slots can still name until `export rotate-escrow` has re-wrapped them all ([Rotate the escrow key](encryption.md#rotate-the-escrow-key)). |

## Metrics

| Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `config.server.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled` | `false` | Create a prometheus-operator ServiceMonitor scraping `/metrics` on port `metrics` (9090) of the Service. Needs the `monitoring.coreos.com` CRDs. |
| `config.server.metrics.serviceMonitor.interval` | `"1m"` | Scrape interval. |
| `config.server.metrics.serviceMonitor.scrapeTimeout` | `"10s"` | Scrape timeout. |
| `config.server.metrics.serviceWide.enabled` | `false` | Add a second ServiceMonitor endpoint scraping the service-wide `/metrics` on port `service-metrics` (9091), with the same interval and timeout. Needs `config.server.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled`. Every replica serves the same values. to scrape only one replica, configure that in your scraper. |
| `config.server.metrics.serviceWide.interval` | null | `VAULT_SYNC_SERVICE_METRICS_INTERVAL`: how often each replica reads the service-wide metrics from PostgreSQL. |

## Export

| Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `config.export.enabled` | `false` | Render the export CronJob. Off by default, so a minimal install needs only the database, S3 and OIDC settings. Turning it on is recommended: the export is the plaintext disaster-recovery copy of every vault. |
| `config.export.schedule` | `"0 3 * * *"` | Cron schedule. |
| `config.export.timeZone` | empty | IANA time zone of the schedule. Empty uses the cluster's default. |
| `config.export.activeDeadlineSeconds` | `21600` | Upper bound, in seconds, on one export run (the Job's `activeDeadlineSeconds`, 6 hours by default). It must be positive. Runs never overlap (`concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`), so a hung export, for example on a stalled NFS volume, would otherwise block every later run. |
| `config.export.output.persistence` | `{}` | The output volume, as a bjw-s persistence item (`type`, `existingClaim`, `server`/`path` for `nfs`, ...), for example `{type: persistentVolumeClaim, existingClaim: vault-sync-export}`, or an `nfs` or `hostPath` volume that your tape-archival tooling reads. Required while the export is enabled. Mounted at `/export` in the export job only; mount options other than the path can be set here. |
| `config.export.output.directory` | `"vaults"` | Directory inside the volume, a single name. The job runs `export -out /export/<directory>`. The export replaces it on every run and keeps a lock file and a staging directory beside it, at the top of the volume. |
| `config.export.database.url.value` | empty | The export's own `VAULT_SYNC_DATABASE_URL`, for example for a read-only role ([the grants it needs](backup-and-restore.md)). Empty uses the server's. Exclusive with `config.export.database.url.secretKeyRef`. |
| `config.export.database.url.secretKeyRef.name` | empty | Secret holding the export's database URL. |
| `config.export.database.url.secretKeyRef.key` | empty | Key of that Secret. |
| `config.export.database.tls.clientCertificate.secretName` | empty | The export's own PostgreSQL client certificate Secret, mounted at `/etc/vault-sync/export-database-client-cert`. Empty uses the server's. The CA (`config.database.tls.caCert`) is always shared. |
| `config.export.database.tls.clientCertificate.certKey` | `"tls.crt"` | Key of the certificate. |
| `config.export.database.tls.clientCertificate.keyKey` | `"tls.key"` | Key of the private key. |
| `config.export.s3.credentials.secretName` | empty | The export's own S3 credentials Secret, for example read-only credentials, mounted at `/etc/vault-sync/export-s3-credentials`. Empty uses `config.s3.credentials`. The bucket, endpoint and CA are shared. |
| `config.export.s3.credentials.accessKeyIdKey` | `"AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID"` | Key of the access key id. |
| `config.export.s3.credentials.secretAccessKeyKey` | `"AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY"` | Key of the secret access key. |
| `config.export.escrow.secretName` | empty | Secret holding the escrow identity (SPEC.md §9.4), mounted read-only at `/etc/vault-sync/escrow` in the export job only, never in the server. The export job reads it to decrypt escrowed vaults. The escrow signing keys never go into the cluster: they stay offline and are used only by a manual escrow key rotation (`export rotate-escrow`, [Rotate the escrow key](encryption.md#rotate-the-escrow-key)), and the chart refuses to render if any controller would get them. |
| `config.export.escrow.key` | `"escrow.key"` | Key of that Secret. It holds the identity file (`age-keygen -pq` output; both identities during an escrow key rotation), which the export job reads as `VAULT_SYNC_ESCROW_IDENTITY_FILE`. The chart refuses to render if any value would put it into the server. |
| `config.escrowJobToken.secretName` | empty | Secret holding the static bearer token of the escrow rotation endpoint (`VAULT_SYNC_ESCROW_JOB_TOKEN_FILE`), mounted read-only at `/etc/vault-sync/escrow-job-token` into the server, which checks it, and the export job, which presents it, and into nothing else. Empty leaves the endpoint off. |
| `config.escrowJobToken.key` | `"token"` | Key of that Secret. It holds one line of at least 32 characters, for example `openssl rand -base64 32`. |

## Route

`config.route` renders a Gateway API HTTPRoute (bjw-s `route.main`) that sends its hostnames to port `http` of the Service. Route only port `http` from outside the cluster. The chart sets the backend and the timeouts, and `resources.route.main` overrides any of it. The route has two rules, both to port `http`:

- `/v1/realtime`: `timeouts.request` and `timeouts.backendRequest` of `0s`, which turns them off. It is a long-lived WebSocket, kept alive by the server's pings every 30 seconds, and a gateway's default request timeout would cut it off.
- `/` (everything else): `timeouts.request` and `timeouts.backendRequest` of `15m`. A `CommitBlob` response starts only once the server has composed the whole blob, which can take up to 10 minutes (SPEC.md §6.2), and its response can then take up to `VAULT_SYNC_WRITE_TIMEOUT` (2 minutes by default) to write. Raise it with `resources.route.main.rules` if you raise the write timeout.

| Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `config.route.enabled` | `false` | Render the HTTPRoute. |
| `config.route.hostnames` | `[]` | Hostnames it matches, for example `[sync.example.com]`. |
| `config.route.parentRefs` | `[]` | The Gateway (and listener) to attach to, as Gateway API `parentRefs` (`name`, `namespace`, `sectionName`, ...), for example `[{name: internet-gateway, namespace: gateway, sectionName: https}]`. |
| `config.route.annotations` | `{}` | Annotations of the HTTPRoute. |
| `config.route.labels` | `{}` | Labels of the HTTPRoute. |

## Grafana dashboards

`config.grafana.dashboards` installs the [dashboards](monitoring.md) (Overview, Server and Dependencies, with the JSON in the chart's `dashboards/` directory, UIDs `vault-sync-overview`, `vault-sync-server` and `vault-sync-dependencies`) as grafana-operator `GrafanaDashboard`s, as ConfigMaps for the Grafana chart's dashboard sidecar, or both. Both are off by default.

| Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `config.grafana.dashboards.enabled` | `false` | Render one grafana-operator `GrafanaDashboard` (`grafana.integreatly.org/v1beta1`) per dashboard, named `<release>-dashboard-<name>`. Needs the grafana-operator CRDs. |
| `config.grafana.dashboards.instanceSelector` | `{}` | Label selector of the `Grafana` resources to import into, for example `{matchLabels: {dashboards: grafana}}`. Required while `config.grafana.dashboards.enabled`. |
| `config.grafana.dashboards.folder` | empty | Title of the Grafana folder to put the dashboards in. At most one of `folder`, `folderRef` and `folderUID`. Setting  more fails the render. |
| `config.grafana.dashboards.folderRef` | empty | Name of a `GrafanaFolder` in the release namespace to put the dashboards in. |
| `config.grafana.dashboards.folderUID` | empty | UID of an existing Grafana folder to put the dashboards in. |
| `config.grafana.dashboards.resyncPeriod` | null (the operator's default) | How often the operator re-applies the dashboards, for example `10m`. |
| `config.grafana.dashboards.allowCrossNamespaceImport` | null (`false`) | Let `Grafana` instances in other namespaces import the dashboards. |
| `config.grafana.dashboards.labels` | `{}` | Extra labels of each `GrafanaDashboard`. |
| `config.grafana.dashboards.configMaps.enabled` | `false` | Render each dashboard as a ConfigMap `<release>-dashboard-<name>` holding `<name>.json`, for the Grafana chart's dashboard sidecar, for deployments without the operator. Independent of `config.grafana.dashboards.enabled`. |
| `config.grafana.dashboards.configMaps.label` | `"grafana_dashboard"` | Label the sidecar watches (the Grafana chart's `sidecar.dashboards.label`). |
| `config.grafana.dashboards.configMaps.labelValue` | `"1"` | Value of that label (`sidecar.dashboards.labelValue`). |
| `config.grafana.dashboards.configMaps.annotations` | `{}` | Annotations of each ConfigMap, for example `{grafana_folder: vault-sync}` with the sidecar's `folderAnnotation` to choose a folder. |

## Alerts

`config.alerts` renders the packaged alerting rules (`deploy/charts/vault-sync/alerts/vault-sync.rules.yaml`) as a prometheus-operator `PrometheusRule` (`monitoring.coreos.com/v1`). [Alerts](alerts.md) lists every alert with its threshold, the reasoning behind it, and a runbook section that says what to check and what to do; The `runbook_url` of each alert points there. To turn on the rules:

```yaml
config:
  server:
    metrics:
      serviceMonitor: {enabled: true}
      serviceWide: {enabled: true}
  alerts:
    prometheusRule:
      enabled: true
      labels:
        release: kube-prometheus-stack   # whatever your Prometheus's ruleSelector matches
```

The service-wide alerts (retention, export, backlogs) read the service-wide metrics, so scrape port `service-metrics` too (`config.server.metrics.serviceWide.enabled`, or your own scrape configuration). Without it, they never fire. Every expression matches the namespace and the job of this release, so two releases in one Prometheus do not mix. With a scraper that labels series differently, set `config.alerts.prometheusRule.selector`.

For example, to page on slow syncs only after 30 minutes above 5 seconds, and to turn on the kube-state-metrics alerts:

```yaml
config:
  alerts:
    rules:
      VaultSyncSyncLatencyHigh: {threshold: 5, for: 30m}
      VaultSyncNoReplicaReady: {enabled: true}
      VaultSyncReplicasUnavailable: {enabled: true}
```

| Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `config.alerts.prometheusRule.enabled` | `false` | Render the PrometheusRule. Needs the `monitoring.coreos.com` CRDs. |
| `config.alerts.prometheusRule.labels` | `{}` | Extra labels of the PrometheusRule, for example the ones your Prometheus's `ruleSelector` matches. |
| `config.alerts.prometheusRule.annotations` | `{}` | Annotations of the PrometheusRule. |
| `config.alerts.prometheusRule.selector.namespace` | `null` | The `namespace` matcher added to every expression. `null` uses the release namespace; an empty string leaves the matcher out. |
| `config.alerts.prometheusRule.selector.job` | `null` | The `job` matcher added to every expression that reads vault-sync's own metrics. `null` uses the Service name (the release name, the ServiceMonitor's `job` label), and an empty string leaves the matcher out. The kube-state-metrics alerts match the namespace and the Deployment name instead. |
| `config.alerts.runbookUrlBase` | `"https://github.com/solidDoWant/vault-sync/blob/master/docs/admin/alerts.md"` | Each alert's `runbook_url` annotation is this followed by `#` and the alert's name in lower case. Empty leaves `runbook_url` out. |
| `config.alerts.rules` | `{}` | Per-alert overrides keyed by alert name, each with `enabled`, `for` (a Prometheus duration), `severity` (`critical` or `warning`) and `threshold` (for alerts that have one, see  [Alerts](alerts.md)). A disabled alert is dropped from the rendered rules, and an unknown name fails the render. `VaultSyncNoReplicaReady` and `VaultSyncReplicasUnavailable` need kube-state-metrics and are off unless enabled here. `VaultSyncExportNotSucceeding` is on while `config.export.enabled`. |

## Overriding the computed resources

Under `resources`, the chart computes these bjw-s entries. Your values are merged over them and win:

| Entry | What the chart sets |
|---|---|
| `resources.controllers.main` | The server Deployment, named after the release: `replicas: 2`, `RollingUpdate` with `maxUnavailable: 0` and `maxSurge: 1`, `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` of `config.server.shutdownDelay` plus `config.server.shutdownTimeout` plus 10 seconds (at least 45, and 45 with the defaults), `automountServiceAccountToken: false`, a startup probe (`/healthz`, up to 10 minutes, so long migrations are not killed), a liveness probe (`/healthz`) and a readiness probe (`/readyz`, every 2 s) on the metrics port. |
| `resources.controllers.export` | The export CronJob `<release>-export` (when `config.export.enabled`): `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid`, `backoffLimit: 2`, `config.export.activeDeadlineSeconds`, and 3 successful and 3 failed Jobs kept. |
| both controllers | Container `main`, image `ghcr.io/soliddowant/vault-sync` at the chart's `appVersion`, user and group `65532` (`runAsNonRoot`, `fsGroup` 65532), a read-only root filesystem, no privilege escalation, all capabilities dropped and the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile. |
| `resources.service.main` | One ClusterIP Service with ports `http` (8080, primary: ingress and route backends resolve to it), `metrics` (9090) and `service-metrics` (9091). Never route to either metrics port from outside the cluster. |
| `resources.serviceMonitor.main` | The ServiceMonitor, when `config.server.metrics.serviceMonitor.enabled`, with a second endpoint for port `service-metrics` when `config.server.metrics.serviceWide.enabled`. |
| `resources.route.main` | The HTTPRoute, when `config.route.enabled`. |
| `resources.persistence.*` | `database-client-cert`, `database-ca`, `s3-credentials`, `s3-ca`, `export-database-client-cert`, `export-s3-credentials`, `escrow` (read-only Secrets, mode `0440`) and `export` (the output volume). |

The chart sets no scheduling or capacity policy, because you could change but not remove anything that it set: no PodDisruptionBudget, no container resources and no topology spread constraints (a pod that declares any opts out of the cluster's default spreading). Set them under `resources`. For example, to run three replicas, pin the image, size the server and add a PodDisruptionBudget:

```yaml
resources:
  controllers:
    main:
      replicas: 3
      containers:
        main:
          image:
            repository: ghcr.io/soliddowant/vault-sync
            tag: 1.2.3
          resources:
            requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 128Mi}
            limits: {memory: 512Mi}
      podDisruptionBudget:
        maxUnavailable: 1
```

The export job's container is `resources.controllers.export.containers.main`, for example `resources.controllers.export.containers.main.resources.limits.memory: 1Gi`. [Replicas and sizing](requirements.md#replicas-and-sizing) gives starting values. Do not give the server a volume that it writes to: replicas must keep no state of their own (SPEC.md §12).

| Value | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `resources.controllers.main` | `{}` | Overrides of the server Deployment, merged over what the chart computes, for example `replicas`, `podDisruptionBudget` or `containers.main.resources`. |
| `resources.ingress` | `{}` | An Ingress, entirely yours. With  one Service, its backend resolves to port `http` without naming a Service. |
